messages:
Maya (solutions): quick heads-up — LiveWire POC demo just failed twice. SSE stream drops after ~12–18s, then the client gets a partial JSON chunk and chokes. Demo recording attached but i pasted the client logs below.

Ben (sales): ugh. repro on our end? env details? which model / plan?

Maya (solutions): hosted API, model=redwood-rlhf-small, auth via bearer token (sts short-lived). Customer on Mac Safari latest. They use our JS SDK in the browser via a proxy. Pricing tier = self-serve but traffic is small — not high QPS.

Ben (sales): ok. tagging eng to triage. @Kavita can you take a look? i'll ping the customer for logs and exact curl.

Kavita (eng): assigning, diving in. couple quick checks: 1) are we seeing 429s or 401s server-side? 2) is the proxy doing any buffering/timeout? 3) any chunk size pattern?

Maya (solutions): paste from client console: 
```
SSE: open
SSE: data chunk (len=132) -> partial json
SSE: unexpected end of stream, parsing failed
SSE: reconnect attempt #1 after 1500ms
fetch error: network failure (no status)
```

Alex (platform): infra observability shows connection from LiveWire IP flapped at ~1987654405 and we saw a burst of 502s from the proxy in front of our edge (nginx) around that time. No 429s from our rate-limiter service, but we do have a short auth-failure spike (401) at 1987654399 tied to token refresh failures.

Kavita (eng): interesting — partial chunks + 502s at proxy + 401s on auth refresh could mean the SDK's token refresh race is triggering a short lived handshake failure, then the proxy tears the upstream connection and forwards a truncated response. Can you share the exact curl the customer used to reproduce?

Maya (solutions): sending reproduction curl in thread: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <short-lived-token>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=redwood-rlhf-small&stream=true"
```

Ben (sales): customer said they also saw this only behind their corporate proxy (BlueGate). Works fine if they bypass the proxy.

Alex (platform): that matches our nginx 502s. BlueGate is probably doing aggressive read-timeouts or buffering then closing the TCP session when it hits some internal limit -> client sees partial chunk. Two-pronged mitigation: 1) ask customer to allow keep-alive + long timeouts for SSE on proxy, 2) make SDK more tolerant (client-side reassembly + resume).

Kavita (eng): on server-side we can add more explicit SSE-friendly headers: `Cache-Control: no-transform` and ensure we set `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and periodic comment heartbeats `:heartbeat\n\n` every 10s. Also we can return explicit `retry:` SSE field to tell clients to attempt faster reconnects. For token refresh races we should fall back to allowing a single in-flight request to continue during short auth refresh windows (tolerate a 401->retry with new token).

Maya (solutions): customer asked if this is a rate limit — they saw `429` in browser network tab once earlier, then later partial chunks. Could rate limiting cause abrupt close?

Kavita (eng): 429 should be a normal JSON response (not SSE), we don't terminate a streaming connection mid-chunk for a rate-limit. If they hit a rate limiter mid-stream their client usually sees a final event with an error. Abrupt close is more consistent with proxy or intermediate gateway closing TCP or an upstream 502/504.

Alex (platform): we pulled tcpdump for that window — SYN/FIN pairs show proxy-initiated FINs after ~15s of inactivity from their side. They have a default idle timeout of 15s. We should advise them to bump it to 60s for SSE endpoints.

Ben (sales): action items for customer-facing message? short and clear pls

Maya (solutions): draft: "Looks like your corporate proxy (BlueGate) is closing idle streams around 15s which causes partial SSE chunks. Please allow long-lived connections for streaming endpoints (idle timeout >= 60s) or enable proxy pass-through for `text/event-stream`. As a workaround, we recommend using the SDK with automatic chunk reassembly and retry enabled." Thoughts?

Kavita (eng): add technical appendix: - send `:heartbeat` comment every 10s server-side - include `retry: 2000` SSE field - client should buffer and wait for `\n\n` to mark end of event, and treat JSON.parse failures as transient and trigger reconnect with exponential backoff (don't discard partial buffer). Example client pseudo: 
```
let buf = '';
onmessage = (chunk) => { buf += chunk; try { const evt = JSON.parse(buf); handle(evt); buf=''; } catch(e) { /* wait for more data */ } }
```

Alex (platform): we can also add a short server-side mitigation toggle in config: `sse-heartbeat=10s` and `sse-allow-auth-race=true` to be rolled out to the hosted fleet — would reduce customer impact quickly. I'll open a small deploy. deploy-bot: please schedule canary.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout for sse-heartbeat change queued (canary: 3 hosts).

Ben (sales): thanks team. i'll send customer the explanation + workaround and ask BlueGate admin to try 60s timeout. Will follow up after they test. :thumbsup:

Maya (solutions): customer replied — they bumped proxy timeout to 90s and the demo completed end-to-end! they still want an SDK fix for graceful reassembly. I'll log a feature request.

Kavita (eng): noted — created tracker ticket INF-1229 for SDK chunk reassembly + token refresh resilience.

Alex (platform): leaving this open until canary passes. last observed at 1987654958, no failures since.

Ben (sales): great — closing after customer confirmation tomorrow. thanks everyone. :party_parrot:
